ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.95 excess distance fare to the rider via the original payment method; send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route compliance record (no formal warning — first such incident); do not record a driver violation, as the trace shows a traffic reason on the replaced stretch (F11, RD-4); do not flag the driver's account (RD-6 not met).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 17.6 km against a 13.3 km optimal route, +4.3 km [F1], and the single off-route segment 09:06–09:16 drove 6.29 km where the optimal route covers 2.26 km [F3]. The trace fixes the chargeable deviation at 4.22 km, over the 1 km tolerance, so RD-1 is satisfied and the case turns on whether the segment is exempt under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2].

Consent: at 09:03, before the segment began, the driver asked "Jam on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Ubi Avenue 2?" [F7] and the rider answered "Sure, no problem." [F8]. Read in context, that "yes" answers a question that named a road — it is an agreement to go via Ubi Avenue 2, a specific named road, not a free-floating "whichever way is faster" choice (the driver's own account in [F10] frames it the same way: "I asked the rider about going via Ubi Avenue 2 and the rider agreed"). The 12 roads driven on the segment [F3] do not include Ubi Avenue 2, and the driver's statement admits "In the end I went by Jalan Eunos instead" [F10]. RD-5's road-name check therefore places the agreement elsewhere, and the segment counts [RD-5].

Both advocates reach the same ground on this segment (named_road_elsewhere → counts), and my own reading of the record agrees; the driver's unilateral substitution of Jalan Eunos for the agreed road is exactly the case RD-5 treats as not covered by the rider's agreement.

The KLE congestion (band 2, 10–19 km/h, 08:48–09:16) [F11] gives a traffic reason on the replaced stretch, so no driver violation is recorded under RD-4; but under RD-2 a traffic reason never exempts the segment, and the amount turns only on whether the rider agreed to the route driven [RD-4][RD-2].

Amount: (4.22 km deviation − 0 km exempt) × $1.4103/km = $5.95 [F4][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded: the multiplier is 1.0× [F5] and the components are base $3.90, distance $24.75, time $6.41, waiting $0.00, platform $1.47 [F6], so only the excess distance fare is refundable, matching the billed figure [F4].

Because the refund is for an uninformed/unauthorised reroute — the rider was told of a reroute via Ubi Avenue 2 but not of the route actually driven [F7][F8][F10] — the driver gets the RD-7 reminder and the notification failure is logged; the trace settles RD-4 as no violation, so no violation is recorded [RD-7][RD-4]. RD-6 is not met: the driver's prior upheld dispute was not a route matter (route: 0) [F17][RD-6]. The amount is under $10 and the dispute is a route deviation, so system resolution is proper [TH-1][TH-2]. Precedent DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute, $3.20) is aligned on the notification duty, though its quantum differs with its own rate and distance [PREC-1].

The rider named no stop and requested no route; his only message agreed to the driver's proposal [F8][F7], and no stop is measured in the segment [F3]. RD-3 does not exempt the segment.

A complete timestamped chat record [F9] proves what was said, not that the ride followed the agreement; the driver's own statement [F10] shows it did not, and RD-5's road-name check governs.

The 'traffic reason, rider informed and agreed → no_action' row of RD-2 requires the rider to have agreed to the route driven; here the agreement was to Ubi Avenue 2 and the Jalan Eunos route was not informed or agreed [F7][F8][F10], so the refund row applies (RD-2, RD-5).

RD-6 requires an upheld deviation against the driver in this case plus a prior upheld route deviation in 90 days; the profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F17], so flag_account is not available.

The RD-7 reminder is appropriate here, but the DISP-2026-0142 precedent cited is a surge-without-notice case, not a route-deviation case; the RD-7 reminder rests on RD-7 itself and on DISP-2026-0089 [RD-7][PREC-1].

The driver's request for no_action fails: the deviation of 4.22 km exceeds the 1 km tolerance [F1][F3][F4] and the consent did not cover the segment driven [F7][F8][F10], so the excess distance fare is refundable under RD-2.
